findings.statement: Dabrafenib elicits stronger transcriptomic effects in BRAF-mutant cell lines compared to KRAS-mutant lines.
RMC-6236 shows greatest effect in KRAS-mutated cell lines, supporting its KRAS-specific action.
Cell line identity, followed by cell cycle phase, are the major drivers of transcriptomic variation in Tahoe-100M, while drug treatment has modest global effects.
Geneformer, pretrained on Genecorpus-30M and fine-tuned with limited task-specific data, consistently improves predictive accuracy across diverse downstream tasks in network biology.
Geneformer-predicted therapeutic targets GSN and PLN are validated as promising for dilated cardiomyopathy by experimental knockout improving contractile stress.
In silico deletion of GATA4 and TBX5 in Geneformer captures cooperative effects on their cobound targets.

GEARS detects emergent genetic interactions (non-additive) with higher precision than baselines.

CPA outperforms scGen on variance and distribution prediction, with 35.85% improvement in variance prediction.

CROP-seq can identify known positive and negative regulators of TCR signaling, including LCK, ZAP70, LAT as activators and PTPN6, PTPN11, EGR3 as repressors.
Dabrafenib elicits stronger transcriptomic effects in BRAF-mutant cell lines compared to KRAS-mutant lines.
RMC-6236 shows greatest effect in KRAS-mutated cell lines, supporting its KRAS-specific action.
Cell line identity, followed by cell cycle phase, are the major drivers of transcriptomic variation in Tahoe-100M, while drug treatment has modest global effects.
Geneformer, pretrained on Genecorpus-30M and fine-tuned with limited task-specific data, consistently improves predictive accuracy across diverse downstream tasks in network biology.
Geneformer-predicted therapeutic targets GSN and PLN are validated as promising for dilated cardiomyopathy by experimental knockout improving contractile stress.
In silico deletion of GATA4 and TBX5 in Geneformer captures cooperative effects on their cobound targets.
GEARS outperforms existing approaches in predicting transcriptional outcomes of both single and multigene perturbations.
GEARS detects emergent genetic interactions (non-additive) with higher precision than baselines.
GEARS can predict outcomes of perturbations involving genes never experimentally perturbed before.
CPA can impute the vast majority (97.6%) of missing combinatorial genetic perturbations in a Perturb-seq experiment.
CPA can predict held-out perturbation combinations with high accuracy, e.g., R2=0.81 for Panobinostat+Alvespimycin.
CPA outperforms scGen on variance and distribution prediction, with 35.85% improvement in variance prediction.
Cell-cycle and cell-subtype covariates explain significant variation and reveal TF-specific effects masked by global cell-state changes.
Perturb-seq enables pooled CRISPR screens with single-cell RNA-seq readout to dissect transcriptional effects of perturbations on genes, programs, and cell states.
TF modules M2 and M4 have opposing effects on BMDC cell states via positive and negative feedback loops.
Pretrained gene embeddings from scFoundation and scGPT did not consistently outperform a linear model using embeddings derived from training data.
None of the deep learning models consistently outperformed the mean prediction or the linear model for single perturbation prediction.
All deep learning models had prediction error substantially higher than the additive baseline for double perturbation prediction.
sci-Plex scales to thousands of independent perturbations and provides single-cell resolution transcriptomic readouts.
HDAC inhibitors induce a transcriptional response consistent with acetyl-CoA depletion, including upregulation of ACSS2, ACLY, and genes involved in citrate metabolism.
Exogenous acetate, pyruvate, or citrate can partially rescue cells from HDAC inhibitor-induced transcriptional trajectory, supporting the acetyl-CoA depletion model.
For genetic single-perturbation prediction, GenePert is optimal when training data is small; CPA and scGPT are preferable when fine-tuning data is large.
All methods performed poorly on population-distribution metrics, particularly Common-DEGs, in genetic perturbation scenarios.
For genetic combined-perturbation prediction, linearModel and scouter perform the best.
scGen accurately predicts single-cell perturbation response out-of-sample across cell types, studies, and species.
scGen captures both shared and cell-type-specific perturbation responses.
GeneCompass can simulate cell fate transitions (e.g., reprogramming and differentiation) via in silico quantitative perturbation and identify key regulatory factors validated by wet-lab experiments.
GeneCompass gene embedding improves gene perturbation prediction in GEARS, reducing MSE by 15.4%, increasing Spearman's rho to 82.0%, and decreasing incorrect direction DEGs by 13.7%.

GeneCompass achieves superior or comparable performance to state-of-the-art models in multiple downstream tasks including cell type annotation, GRN inference, drug dose response prediction, gene expression profiling, and gene dosage sensitivity prediction.
